_about: Data the phone/desktop app and the Roku app both use. Edit it here, run `python shared/generate.py`, and commit the result: that writes lib/src/generated/app_data.dart and roku/app/source/generated/app_data.brs (and the Roku's icon images come from `icon` via roku/tools/make_assets.py). CI fails if the generated files are out of date. See DESIGN_NOTES.md, "Keeping the apps in sync".

sports._about: By the API's sport id. `name` overrides the API's name (we say Soccer and Football); `icon` is a Material icon name (Flutter's Icons.<name>).

sources._about: Stream sources, best first: streams are grouped by source in this order, and sources not listed go last in the order the API gives them. `nested`: the embed page frames another site's page, which frames the real embed.st player page; the apps find that page and play it directly (see DESIGN_NOTES, Nested-iframe sources). Descriptions are the site's own wording from its watch pages (last checked 2026-09-20). Sources not served at the moment are kept; they have come and gone before.

player._about: Player numbers both apps follow. rowThisGame / rowRecent: how many cards each side of the streams row shows. recentsKept: how many recent games are remembered (finished ones are dropped when the row is shown). stuckDownloadMs: a segment download still running this long (and, on phone/desktop, receiving nothing) gets a second copy. overlayPercent: how opaque the black behind the player's overlays is (title bar, streams pill and row, fallback note), the same for all of them. Phone and desktop only, switching between a source's separate quality feeds (the TV has the bandwidth and stays on the best): downPercent, down when segments download in under this much of their length's time (110: barely keeping up); upPercent, up once they'd download this much faster than needed on the better feed for upHoldMs straight (doubled after an up that didn't hold). slowStartMs: how long a stream may take to start before the spinner says why.

updates._about: How often the apps look for a newer release while running: the Roku on a timer, the desktop app on Home only (when its window gets focus, and on coming back to Home). Android updates through Obtainium.

layout._about: Screen spacing, in pixels of a 1920-wide screen: the Roku draws at exactly that, and the desktop app (which scales its 1360-wide layout to the window) takes the same share of the width. margin: either side of the TV's screen, wide to stay clear of a TV's cropped edges. desktopMargin: the desktop's, smaller (a monitor shows its edges), both beside and above the screen's title, as the TV's title sits about as far from the top as from the side. gap: between cards side by side. sectionGap: above each section's heading.

playerIcons._about: The player's icons, the same on every app (Material icon names, as for sports). streamsPill: a row of cards, what the pill opens, rather than an arrow for which way (a press on the Roku, a tap elsewhere). switched: the note after falling back. weakConnection: the note when the connection can't keep up and there's no lower quality (phone and desktop).

playerText._about: The player's wording, the same on every app. {stream} is a stream's name and HD/SD, e.g. "Delta 1 (HD)"; {quality} a feed's resolution, e.g. "540p". switching*, weakConnection and slow* are phone and desktop only (see player).
playerText.slowConnection: Still loading · your connection is slow
playerText.slowSource: Still loading · the stream is slow to respond

palette._about: Colours both apps draw with. `dark` is the dark theme (the Roku's only one); `light`, where given, is the phone/desktop light theme's version of the same colour.
